summary:
Japan’s December 7, 1941, surprise attack on Pearl Harbor in Oahu, Hawaii, brought the United States into World War II. Japan aimed to disable the US Pacific Fleet so it could expand into Southeast Asia without American interference.

Aircraft launched from six Japanese carriers attacked the naval base in two waves. The strike damaged or sank all eight US battleships present, destroyed more than 180 aircraft, and killed 2,403 Americans. Japan also attacked US and British territories across the Pacific and Southeast Asia. The three US aircraft carriers assigned to Pearl Harbor were at sea, and key oil storage and repair facilities were left untouched.

Japan’s leaders hoped the attack would enable rapid territorial gains and lead to a negotiated peace. Instead, the United States declared war on Japan on December 8. Germany and Italy declared war on the United States three days later, and the United States responded in kind. The attack was widely seen in America as unprovoked, despite the tensions and negotiations that preceded it.
